captions.detailed: A realistic model of an articulated desktop globe. It features a dark brown circular wooden base, a brass-colored metallic support stand and semi-circular meridian ring, and a blue spherical globe with simplified beige continents. The globe sphere is mounted within the meridian ring and is designed to rotate continuously around its tilted polar axis.
captions.instruction: Generate a realistic, articulated desktop globe. The model should include a broad dark brown circular base, a brass-colored vertical spindle supporting a semi-circular meridian arm, and a blue sphere representing the globe with stylized beige landmasses. Make sure the globe is articulated to rotate freely on its polar axis within the meridian arm.
captions.factory: The code constructs the model in three main parts: a base, a meridian arm, and the globe sphere. The base is created by combining a flat cylindrical base plate with a vertical support spindle using cylinder primitives. The meridian arm is modeled as a sweep or a ring segment (using torus or cylinder subtraction) and joined to the spindle. The globe is constructed as a sphere primitive, decorated with smaller offset spherical patches or cylinders representing continents, and is connected to the meridian arm via a continuous rotational joint aligned with the earth's tilt angle.
